zodiacal.notes: ORIENTATION: rows = ecliptic latitude beta (0,5,10,15,20,25,30,45,60,75 deg), cols = helioecliptic longitude difference lambda-lambda_sun (0..180 deg, 19 steps). UNITS/TABLE NUMBER: these are the values of Leinert et al. 1998 TABLE 16, in S10_sun units (solar-type stars of 10th visual magnitude per square degree, 'S10sun(vis)'), at 500 nm, annually averaged, for observation from Earth at 1 AU; adapted/updated from Levasseur-Regourd & Dumont (1980). IMPORTANT UNIT CLARIFICATION: the grid most often reproduced in ETCs/calculators (11500 at dlon=15,beta=0; 230 gegenschein; 77 pole) is Leinert TABLE 17, which is THE IDENTICAL TABLE converted to physical units: Table17[1e-8 W m-2 sr-1 um-1 at 0.50 um] = Table16[S10_sun] x 1.28 (verified cell-by-cell, 0 mismatches >2%; e.g. 9000->11500, 180->230). Many secondary sources mislabel Table 17's SI numbers as 'S10'. ECLIPTIC POLE: 60 +/- 3 S10_sun (= 77e-8 W m-2 sr-1 um-1 in Table 17 caption). BLANK CELLS NEAR SUN: the print leaves 8 cells empty (no dash, just blank) where the sky is unobservably close to the Sun: dlon=0 and 5 at beta=0,5,10, and dlon=10 at beta=0,5; encoded here as -1. Ground data originally limited to elongation>30 deg; Leinert extended the table inward to ~15 deg elongation using Helios A/B (Leinert et al. 1982) and rocket (Leinert et al. 1976) photometry, with additional smoothing. Quoted brightness errors: 10-15 S10_sun for low values, larger for the highest brightnesses. Smooth interpolation between nodes is endorsed by the authors. CROSS-CHECKS: (1) publisher full-text HTML table (node8.html) parsed programmatically; (2) skysim (dkirkby/skysim, zodiacal.py) independent digitization of Table 17 - exact match on all 190 cells incl. blank positions; (3) unit-symbol caption images (img51/img226/img227.gif) read at high zoom to confirm S10_sun, the 1.28e-8 factor, and the 77e-8 pole value. VizieR J/A+AS/127/1 does NOT contain these tables in machine-readable form (only refs + 2 IRAS FITS maps).

starlight.notes: SOURCE: Leinert et al. 1998, A&AS 127, 1, Sect. 10.4, TABLE 35 - 'Pioneer 10 background starlight in blue (440 nm), given in galactic coordinates and S10_sun units. From Toller (1981)' (Pioneer 10/11 imaging photopolarimeter; Toller 1981 PhD thesis; see also Toller, Tanabe & Weinberg 1987). BAND: blue, 440 nm (B-like), NOT V; Leinert Table 36 gives the companion red 640 nm grid (same layout) if a more V-like band is needed. UNITS: S10_sun (solar-type 10th-mag stars per deg^2; the caption uses the same S10_sun symbol image as zodiacal Table 16; Gordon et al. 1998 call the same Pioneer unit S10(G2V)). At 440 nm, 1 S10_sun = 1.19e-8 W m-2 sr-1 um-1 = 0.550 S10(A0-based) (Leinert Table 2). DGL: INCLUDED - maps taken beyond 2.8 AU where zodiacal light is undetectable, so the measurement is 'background starlight, including some diffuse galactic light, observed directly'; individually resolved stars brighter than ~6.5 mag were removed using a 12457-star catalog, so bright-star light is NOT included. ORIENTATION: rows = galactic latitude b (-80,-70,-60,-50,-40,-30,-24,-20,-16,-12,-8,-4,0,4,8,12,16,20,24,30,40,50,60,70,80 deg; note finer 4-deg steps within |b|<=24), cols = galactic longitude l = 0..350 deg in 10-deg steps. This IS the full published lon x lat grid (not a latitude-binned average). MISSING CELLS: -1 marks the 28 cells of the region Pioneer did not map (roughly l=170-240 deg at b=+16..+50; printed as dashes or left blank in the original). TRANSCRIPTION: digitized from the publisher's page scan (img403.gif, 870x591) - no machine-readable copy exists at VizieR or in surveyed software (skysim, IACT NSB codes use Gaia instead); every cell was read in at least two independent magnified renderings (3x tiles, 5x gridded per-cell tiles with synthetic headers) and all ~30 discrepancies adjudicated at 12-20x zoom; tesseract and Apple Vision OCR both failed on the degraded bitmap font, so values rest on careful visual transcription - treat isolated +/-1-digit ambiguities in a handful of cells as possible at the few-cell level. FIDELITY ANCHORS: LMC appears as 213 S10_sun at (l=280,b=-30) vs ~60-80 neighbors; galactic plane (b=0) median 230 vs |b|=80 median 29 S10_sun, consistent with Table 34 pole values; Milky Way bulge/Carina/Cygnus enhancements present at l~0/280-310/60-80. Quoted accuracy of the Pioneer photometry is ~10%.
